originality.rationale: The 2026 full text defines the sign and investigates numerical/order-parameter prediction rather than exact sign word laws. The readable original 2000 paper treats phase ordering and transitions, without a stationary Markov transition matrix or all-T variance. The 2023 symbolic-dynamics review computes 3-point ordinal frequencies (which already imply pairwise sign frequencies), not the conditional distribution at arbitrary lag or exact all-window generating functions. Known prior direction-fiber Hausdorff dimension and typical minus frequency are not enough to imply stationarity Markovity or a complete product law. Search results provided no direct exact duplicate; this is a bounded literature assessment, not proof of worldwide novelty. The full 2002 crisis paper was inaccessible, so a residual priority risk is stated.
residual_risks: Older specialized papers on ordinal codings or finite-state Markov partitions may already state this exact finite-window law.
Complete primary text of Shrimali--Ramaswamy (2002) was unavailable, so its detailed results are not ruled out.

value.rationale: The 2026 directional-phase prediction study measures finite-time M but provides no exact sampling null law. Here the entire finite-length distribution of the *same* natural derivative-free sign observable is determined, allowing exact counts, covariance sign alternation, and uncertainty calibration for all window lengths. The partition is nontrivial: it merges branches of the tent map, yet the directional observation remains exactly memory-one. This is a natural finite-dimensional statistical classification, not merely the already-known mean or impossibility of adjacent negatives. No global transition or learning-performance claims are made.
